target_year_over_year_context.explanation: Both groups define the scope, market segments, and product portfolio of the Storage Business Unit (SBU). 2023 D027/D030 detail SBU's inclusion of SSDs and components for enterprise/cloud, client, and consumer markets, specifically listing product series (5300, 7450, etc.) and NAND layers (176/232). 2024 D039 similarly defines SBU's scope into data center, PC, and consumer markets with SSDs and components, maintaining the same specific topic of SBU definition and portfolio. Other IDs in the proposed group (mu_2024_1_D016, D020, D040, D042) describe different aspects (e.g., revenue, specific product launches) or are unrelated to the core SBU definition scope provided by D039, so they are excluded to ensure topic specificity. mu_2023_1_D027 and D030 are kept together as they jointly describe the SBU scope and products in 2023.

comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's four reportable segments are Data Center, Client, Gaming, and Embedded, each encompassing specific product lines for data centers, client devices, gaming hardware, and embedded solutions.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD define their business structures by specific end-market segments involving data center and PC/client hardware. MU's Storage Business Unit (SBU) supplies SSDs to the data center, PC, and consumer markets, explicitly listing enterprise SSDs for data centers and client SSDs for PCs. Similarly, AMD defines its Data Center segment as supplying server products for data centers and its Client segment as supplying CPUs and APUs for desktops and notebooks. While MU focuses on storage components within these markets, AMD focuses on processing logic, but both disclose product portfolios segmented by these identical core infrastructure and end-user markets.

sentences.text: SBU includes SSDs and component-level storage solutions sold into the data center, PC, and consumer markets.
The data center market includes enterprise and cloud SSDs and enterprise NAND components while the PC market consists of client SSDs.
• the Data Center segment, which primarily includes AI accelerators, server CPUs, GPUs, APUs, DPUs, FPGAs, SmartNICs, and Adaptive SoC products for data centers;
• the Client segment, which primarily includes CPUs, APUs, and chipsets for desktops and notebooks;
